4. Let us take up the issue by adverting to Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which reads as under:-
"Appeal to High Court.-(1) The Requiring Body or any person aggrieved by the Award passed by an Authority under section 69 may file an appeal to the High Court within sixty Patna High Court COMPAN.

sentences.text: APL No.1 of 2022(6) dt.19-07-2023 days from the date of Award:

Provided that the High Court may, if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the said period, allow it to be filed within a further period not exceeding sixty days.

(2) Every appeal referred to under sub-section (1) shall be heard as expeditiously as possible and endeavor shall be made to dispose of such appeal within six months from the date on which the appeal is presented to the High Court.
Explanation:- For the purposes of this section, "High Court" means the High Court within the jurisdiction of which the land acquired or proposed to be acquired is situated."
5.

It is apparent from a plain reading of the Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 that it provides for an appeal but it does not use the word First Appeal or Compensation Appeal or Miscellaneous Appeal.
6.

It is relevant to quote here Section 70 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which reads as under:-
"Form of Award-(1) Every Award under this Chapter shall be in Patna High Court COMPAN. APL No.1 of 2022(6) dt.19-07-2023 writing signed by the Presiding Officer of the Authority, and shall specify the amount awarded under clause first of section 28, and also the amounts (if any) respectively awarded under each of the other clauses of the same subsection, together with the grounds of awarding each of the said amounts.

sentences.text: (2) Every such Award shall be deemed to be a decree and the statement of the grounds of every such Award a judgment within the meaning of clause (2), and clause (9) of respectively, of section 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908)."
7. Thus, the Award passed under Section 69 arising out of the proceeding is deemed to be a decree within the meaning of Clause 2 and Clause 9 respectively of Section 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
8. It is clear that the Award of the LARR Authority has been recognized to be a decree in clear terms under Section 70 of the LARR Act.
It is, thus, clear that the Award of the LARR Authority is a decree and it can be a decree within the meaning of Section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
Hence, the Award of the LARR Authority could be construed to be a decree.

Therefore, appeal under Section 74 arising out of Section 69 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act would Patna High Court COMPAN.
